title: The Term Struct
description: term.h defines the C struct for a lambda term: one struct with a kind field covers a variable, a lambda, and an application.

steps.description: This is `term.h`, the header for the C reducer. The page says a term is a variable, a lambda, or an application, so one struct with a `kind` covers all three. The first two lines are the include guard, which stops the header from being included twice. `Kind` is an enum with three values: `VAR`, `LAM`, and `APP`, one per term shape.

`Term` is the struct. `kind` records which shape this term is. `name` holds the variable for a `VAR` or the bound variable for a `LAM`. `a` and `b` hold children: for a `LAM`, `a` is the body; for an `APP`, `a` is the function and `b` is the argument.
